expect:
Two marks per developed explanation.
• Plainchant (Gregorian chant) is the oldest musical tradition of the Catholic Church — unaccompanied choral singing in Latin that dates from the medieval period. It is used in liturgy to enhance the prayerful atmosphere and to elevate the congregation's attention towards God. The Catechism (CCC 2501) affirms that sacred art serves to evoke the transcendent mystery of God.
• Mystery plays and passion plays are dramatic performances depicting biblical events or the Passion of Christ. They were especially important in the medieval period for communicating the Gospel to people who could not read, and passion plays (performed during Holy Week) continue today as a way of helping communities meditate on the Paschal Mystery.
